summary.intent: Fix the FirstRun planner using a neatlogs-derived fix: replace the system prompt, add code guards against invented/no-op/fake-secret steps, add a deterministic plan cache, add tests, and commit.
summary.outcome: Committed 3ca6f11 with a new prompt (PROMPT_VERSION 2), guards, a plan cache and a new test file. The full suite passed (175 passed, 24 skipped, 1 xfailed). The neatlogs trace and triage data were empty or unavailable, so the fix was based on the saved investigation file and v1 outputs were not replayed.

repo: Planner fix lives in src/firstrun/planner.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT, PROMPT_VERSION, guard logic and plan cache keyed by sha256(docs markdown + prompt version) in RUNS_DIR/.plan_cache.
Cache is only used when no llm is injected, so tests and replays never touch it; FIRSTRUN_REPLAN=1 bypasses it.
tests/test_edge_planner.py had 3 tests whose docs text lacked the commands, so they broke once the guards required commands to appear in the docs.
Skipped_out_of_scope steps are not guarded because they never run.
A `&&` chain counts as in the docs when every part appears there.
Files from a dropped step are merged into the next kept step so a later `python <file>` still finds them.
The Entire hook adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to commits automatically.
workflow: Python-in-bash heredocs with escapes broke on quoting and wrote real newlines into string literals. Using the Edit tool for source edits was more reliable.
neatlogs search_traces with `fields` failed with not_enabled (NL-1923 rollout), and a retry filtered by detection name returned 0 results.
triage_list returned 0 cards, so triage_update_status was not applicable.

friction: Bash heredoc quoting broke the first attempt to apply planner changes.
A scripted test rewrite put real newlines into string literals in test_edge_planner.py, which needed manual repair.
neatlogs trace search was disabled or empty, so no planner spans could be inspected.
The first guard loop lost files from dropped steps and needed a rewrite.
open_items: Replay the 3 v1 planner outputs, or run firstrun on the Chroma page, to see real guard_dropped counts in neatlogs.
The lead should resolve the triage item after v2 proves the fix. No triage item existed, so none was moved to in_progress.
I added a neatlogs.planner.guard_rewritten attribute that the spec did not ask for.
